page.layout: Two printed pages on this scan. Left: a fragment of the facing page's outer margin, cut at the spine, with short notes. Right: running head "PARS II.", page number at top right, a continued italic passage of text, a paragraph, and a row of numbers at the foot of the text block.; One printed page, main text in one column at centre-right; a fragment of a left-hand column of marginal text at the far left edge; faint show-through from the other side not transcribed.

p.i: dibus tredecim à primo distantem, ita colligenda, ut quolibet excursu nō nisi unicū auferre liceat. Quæritur, quantum itineris dicta lege omnibus congestis, conficiatur?

Hoc ludi cursorij genus juuenes nonnunquam instī-tuere solent, dum alteri duorum certus numerus, fracto nullo, comportandus, alteri interim facto ad designatum locum excursu, redeundū, ut qui pensum suum primò absoluerit, βραβεῖον auferat. Quæstio igitur hic de Arithmeticae progressionis summa.

main_text.p: Extremus simuluterq; est 113, factus ex eo per extremi terminì nomen 3390, cuius dimidium 1695 pedes, faciētes 339 passus Geometricos. Tantùm spatiū excurrendo conficit, idemq; recurrendo repetit, quare duplum primò inuentum, 3390 pedes, uel 678 gressus quæsitum explicant.
main_text.head: CAPVT III.

page.notes: Left-page fragments at the spine, cut off and only partly legible: "efsio", "allelo", "st 60,", "midiu", "resio", "a.", "lustre". Their position relative to the left text block is uncertain. The page number "35" is doubtful; the scan shows it mirrored or smudged. The Greek word "βραβεῖον" is read with doubt from the scan. The right part of the page is cut off and continues in part 2. The leftmost strip holds fragments of marginal notes (e.g. "ab uno", "uiccsi", "redien", "orolo", "4 ulti", "midium", "dibus"); they are cut off and only partly legible, so they are not transcribed. Show-through text in the lower area is not transcribed. The heading "CAPVT" is printed with a Roman numeral "III" in the header-like line; the reading is uncertain.
